content:
Marta Kowal-Brandt
marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role at Corvale Mobility. I am a QA automation engineer with seven years of experience, including two years focused largely on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. I am seeking to move into DevOps or platform engineering full time, building on my experience supporting product teams with infrastructure and automation.

At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams, covering builds, testing and artifact publishing. I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and moving end-to-end tests to on-demand environments. I also built merge-request test environments using Docker Compose and later Helm charts on a shared Kubernetes cluster. This work has given me practical experience making development and testing workflows more efficient for backend and product teams.

Corvale’s fleet connectivity project brings together infrastructure and backend services to support a new generation of trains. I would bring experience with Linux, Python and Bash, as well as a testing background grounded in reliability: I maintain an approximately 900-test end-to-end suite and helped reduce its flaky test rate from 7% to under 1%. My ownership of pipelines across three teams also aligns with Corvale’s emphasis on collaboration and end-to-end ownership.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my test infrastructure and CI/CD experience could contribute to the fleet connectivity team. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It presents credible quantified achievements: reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and reducing flaky tests from 7% to under 1%. The progression from QA automation into test infrastructure and CI/CD is explained honestly, and the letter avoids claiming Terraform, AWS, networking, or security experience that is not present in the candidate information. The main content weakness is that it gives limited evidence of systems design, stakeholder engagement, or broader infrastructure operation, which are central to this role. One phrase also overstates the source material by referring to backend teams.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in plain-text form, with standard headings, readable paragraphs, and relevant terms including CI/CD, GitLab CI, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, Linux, Python, Bash, and test environments. It is likely to parse correctly. However, AI and ATS screening probability for this particular role is moderate to low because the letter does not contain the job's core terms Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS, infrastructure as code, systems architecture, networking, mTLS, SSL/TLS, or security. These are genuine candidate-background gaps rather than terms that should be added without evidence. The existing wording could also use the exact supported phrase "shared Kubernetes cluster" more prominently.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's infrastructure automation, CI/CD, reliability, Linux, Python, collaboration, and ownership themes. The candidate demonstrates hands-on work building ephemeral environments and operating pipelines across three product teams. The quantified reliability and efficiency results support the analytical-thinking requirement. The document does not establish strong Terraform/Terragrunt experience, AWS or another major cloud, systems architecture and system design, networking including mTLS and SSL/TLS, practical security awareness, IoT or remote-device integration, or virtual-machine experience. It also provides only limited direct evidence of leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along. Java is present only as test code, so the JVM backend/full-stack nice-to-have is not demonstrated. These are profile gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting the letter.
critique.improvement_instructions: CRITICAL: In the third paragraph, replace the sentence "This work has given me practical experience making development and testing workflows more efficient for backend and product teams." The original candidate information supports product teams, but does not establish work with backend teams. Use a truthful version such as: "This work has given me practical experience making development and testing workflows more efficient for three product teams and approximately 25 developers."\n\nMINOR: To strengthen the analytical-thinking evidence without adding unsupported skills, insert one concise sentence after the paragraph describing the 900-test suite: "Earlier in my career, I also investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers." This uses documented experience and gives the recruiter a clearer example of analytical troubleshooting.
critique.critical_issues:
Potential unsupported claim: the cover letter says the candidate improved workflows for "backend and product teams," but the original candidate information supports ownership for three product teams and approximately 25 developers, not backend-team experience. Remove or correct "backend teams" to prevent this from being interpreted as a hallucinated background claim.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "making development and testing workflows more efficient for backend and product teams"

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role at Corvale Mobility. I am a QA automation engineer with seven years of experience, including two years focused largely on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. I am seeking to move into DevOps or platform engineering full time, building on my experience supporting product teams with infrastructure and automation.

At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams, covering builds, testing and artifact publishing. I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and moving end-to-end tests to on-demand environments. I also built merge-request test environments using Docker Compose and later Helm charts on a shared Kubernetes cluster. This work has given me practical experience making development and testing workflows more efficient for three product teams and approximately 25 developers.

Corvale’s fleet connectivity project brings together infrastructure and backend services to support a new generation of trains. I would bring experience with Linux, Python and Bash, as well as a testing background grounded in reliability: I maintain an approximately 900-test end-to-end suite and helped reduce its flaky test rate from 7% to under 1%. My ownership of pipelines across three teams also aligns with Corvale’s emphasis on collaboration and end-to-end ownership.

Earlier in my career, I also investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my test infrastructure and CI/CD experience could contribute to the fleet connectivity team. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It uses specific achievements effectively, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, supporting three product teams, and reducing flaky tests from 7% to under 1%. The letter also explains the candidate's transition toward DevOps without overstating experience. Its main weakness is that the role is infrastructure-focused, while the letter understandably emphasizes QA automation and test infrastructure rather than the job's central architecture, Terraform, networking, security, and cloud-operation requirements.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly: it uses standard text formatting, a conventional greeting and closing, readable paragraphs, and relevant keywords such as CI/CD, GitLab CI, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, Linux, Python, Bash, and PostgreSQL. Keyword coverage is limited for the role because Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS, systems architecture, networking, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and security are not present. These are genuine experience gaps in the supplied candidate information, not terms that should be added without evidence. AI screening probability is moderate: the measurable achievements and infrastructure terminology support relevance, but the absence of several core requirements will likely reduce ranking for this particular role.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's infrastructure-adjacent work: CI/CD ownership, ephemeral environments, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, Linux, scripting, reliability, analytical problem-solving, and support for multiple product teams. It also reflects Corvale's emphasis on collaboration and end-to-end ownership to a limited extent. However, the candidate's material does not demonstrate strong Terraform/Terragrunt experience, cloud design and operation, systems architecture, networking or mTLS/SSL/TLS, practical security, AWS, IoT or remote-device integration, stakeholder-led technical proposals, or virtual-machine experience. The candidate has Java experience only in test code, not the backend/JVM background described as a nice-to-have.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the second paragraph, change “moving end-to-end tests to on-demand environments” to “moving end-to-end tests to on-demand ephemeral environments” so the wording matches the candidate's documented experience and uses the job's infrastructure terminology more precisely.

2. In the third paragraph, change “helped reduce its flaky test rate from 7% to under 1%” to “reduced its flaky test rate from 7% to under 1%.” The original candidate information supports direct ownership of this result, so the stronger wording is both accurate and more impactful.

3. In the second paragraph, replace the final sentence, “This work has given me practical experience making development and testing workflows more efficient for three product teams and approximately 25 developers,” with “This work involved end-to-end ownership of development and testing infrastructure for three product teams and approximately 25 developers.” This uses the employer's ownership language while remaining supported by the documented responsibility for the pipelines and environments.

4. In the third paragraph, replace the broad phrase “a testing background grounded in reliability” with the more concrete wording “a reliability-focused test infrastructure background.” This more directly connects the candidate's documented flaky-test reduction and pipeline work to the role's emphasis on reliable platforms without claiming unsupported production-platform experience.
